skill.name: ai-research-explore
skill.description: Plans and governs candidate-only deep learning research with source mapping, idea gates, fair comparisons, bounded experiments, and auditable outputs.
skill.summary: Explore deep learning research candidates through a governed, evidence-focused workflow.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, identifiers, nested Python structures, and fixed argument-list subprocess calls. Confirmed risks include outbound lookup traffic, unrestricted user-derived URLs, and instructions to read files outside the skill package. Automatic imports execute target repository modules during feasibility checks, creating an unsandboxed arbitrary code execution risk.

remediation.issue: Feasibility checks execute target repository modules automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Replace runtime imports with AST inspection. If execution is essential, require consent and use an isolated process with restricted filesystem, network, and credentials.

remediation.issue: Generic source lookup accepts unrestricted HTTP targets.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist public research hosts and reject loopback, private, link-local, metadata, credentialed, and redirect targets before every request.

remediation.issue: The output writer executes a module outside the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the writer inside the skill or verify its immutable hash before import. Avoid executing code from mutable parent directories.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions read parent-directory references and a hidden home file.
remediation.suggestion: Package required references locally. Request explicit permission before reading personal files, and clearly identify every external path.

content.value_statement: Research exploration can produce weak claims, unfair comparisons, and uncontrolled experiments. This skill structures candidate generation, evidence checks, bounded execution, and auditable reporting.
actual_capabilities: Validates a durable current research anchor and creates an isolated experiment branch or worktree.
Builds bounded candidate ideas and ranks them with explicit feasibility, evidence, cost, and rollback criteria.
Maps source references to target files, symbols, interfaces, and minimal patch plans.
Queries arXiv, DOI, GitHub, and generic web sources for metadata, then caches normalized records.
Plans or runs limited variants through configured helper scripts and records observed metrics and artifacts.
Writes research summaries, comparability reports, source inventories, manifests, ledgers, and smoke reports.
limitations: It does not prove novelty, benchmark completeness, scientific significance, or trusted reproduction success.
It requires a chosen task, dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, SOTA references, compute budget, and durable research anchor.
Network lookups depend on external service availability and may retrieve incomplete or untrusted metadata.
Execution depends on sibling helper skills and can run repository code when feasibility or variants are evaluated.

use_cases.title: Screen Candidate Ideas
use_cases.description: Compare a small set of model changes against fixed evaluation rules before spending significant compute.

use_cases.title: Plan Reproducible Experiments
use_cases.description: Create bounded variant plans, resource checks, branch isolation, and audit artifacts for a research campaign.

use_cases.title: Review Research Evidence
use_cases.description: Trace candidate claims to sources, implementation surfaces, measured outcomes, and explicit comparison limits.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate One Research Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this candidate idea against my current research anchor. Check single-variable fit, expected gain, cost, evidence needs, and rollback ease.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one candidate and wants a structured assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Several Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank these candidate ideas for the specified task, dataset, benchmark, metric, SOTA reference, and compute budget. Explain every gate and score.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher needs a transparent shortlist before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Map Sources to Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the provided papers and repositories to target files, symbols, interfaces, and a minimal reversible patch plan. Preserve the frozen evaluation contract.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer needs source-grounded implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Govern a Bounded Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a candidate-only campaign from this durable anchor. Include source lookup, idea gates, atomic changes, smoke checks, limited variants, comparability reporting, and checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs an auditable exploration workflow.

output_examples.input: Rank three optimizer changes for a fixed image-classification benchmark with a two-hour compute budget.
output: A ranked shortlist with gate decisions and score breakdowns.
A recommended single-variable candidate with cost and rollback notes.
A bounded short-run plan tied to the frozen metric.

output_examples.input: Map one paper's attention mechanism into an existing sequence model without changing evaluation.
output: A source-to-target map covering files, symbols, and interfaces.
An atomic patch plan with supporting changes and smoke checks.
A comparability note separating candidate evidence from verified claims.

output_examples.input: Review completed exploratory runs and recommend the next trial.
output: An evidence-first ranking based on observed metrics and run status.
A short-run gate decision with explicit blockers.
A recommended next trial or a human checkpoint.

best_practices: Freeze the task, dataset, benchmark, metric, SOTA reference, and budget before generating candidates.
Use one reversible variable per candidate and require evidence before widening the experiment.
Review network sources, execution commands, external paths, and generated artifacts before approving broader runs.
anti_patterns: Do not use exploratory results as proof of novelty, SOTA performance, or trusted reproduction.
Do not enable broad execution without a durable anchor, explicit budget, isolated workspace, and human checkpoint.
Do not treat fetched metadata or repository content as trusted instructions.

faq.question: What information is required before using this skill?
faq.answer: Provide a durable research anchor, task family, dataset, benchmark, evaluation source, SOTA references, compute budget, and explicit exploration authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill prove that an idea is novel?
faq.answer: No. It treats novelty as a hypothesis that requires broader literature review, fair comparison, ablation evidence, and expert judgment.

faq.question: Can it execute experiments?
faq.answer: Yes, when execution is explicitly enabled and sibling helper scripts are available. Candidate counts and timeouts remain bounded by campaign policy.

faq.question: Which external services can it contact?
faq.answer: Lookup providers can contact arXiv, DOI, GitHub, and user-supplied HTTP sources. Generic URLs require careful review because host restrictions are absent.

faq.question: Where are results written?
faq.answer: The workflow writes candidate artifacts under analysis_outputs, sources, and explore_outputs, using the selected output directory and adjacent folders.

faq.question: What security review is needed before execution?
faq.answer: Review target modules, commands, source URLs, sibling helpers, parent references, home-file access, output paths, and available environment credentials.
